{{Quote|The Sluis sector is a large expanse of sparsely populated space, renowned for its mineral resources and processing facilities. Its primary system, Sluis Van, maintains a formidable shipyard for construction and maintenance. The Praesitlyn system is home to a major HoloNet and subspace communications hub, and the Jedi order maintains a training enclave on Bpfassh.|[[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]]|<ref name="HNN49" />}}
The '''Sluis sector''' {{Pronounced|'slu.i}}, also known as the '''Sluissi sector''', was in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. [[Planet/Legends|Planets]] in the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] included [[Agora]], [[Bpfassh]], [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]], [[Denab/Legends|Denab]], [[Kerest/Legends|Kerest]], [[Orto/Legends|Orto]], [[Praesitlyn/Legends|Praesitlyn]] and [[Sluis Van/Legends|Sluis Van]]. The sector was scouted by [[Keog Boorn]]. The Sluis sector bordered the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]].

==History==
{{Quote|The events now taking place in the Sluis sector shall be resolved. When they are, someone will be needed to oversee the Republic's interests there. Let me be frank: an appointment as ambassador plenipotentiary can be highly profitable.|[[Sly Moore/Legends|Sly Moore]], influencing [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Jannie Ha'Nook]]|<ref name="JT" />}}
The Sluis sector was represented by [[Bor Gracus]] and later by [[Corlissi Ludar]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], and by [[Zilar]] in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]]. The leader of the sector was titled a [[Khedive]].

The sector withdrew from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] to join the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Its [[Senator/Legends|senator]] at that time was Corlissi Ludar.<ref name="HNN49" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] a group of [[Bpfasshi/Legends|Bpfasshi]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] led a rampage of terror and destruction throughout the sector, primarily centered around the [[Bpfassh system/Legends|Bpfassh system]]. They were stopped by a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] task force led by [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]].

During his [[Thrawn campaign|campaign]], [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] launched [[Hit-and-hype raiding|hit-and-fade]] attacks on a trio of [[Star system/Legends|systems]] in Sluis sector, [[Attack on Bpfassh|including the Bpfassh system]].<ref name="EGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] believed the names of the other two systems were "unpronounceable."<ref name="HttE">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref>

{{Sec-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] incorrectly places [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]], [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]], [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]], [[Umgul/Legends|Umgul]], and [[Dac/Legends|Dac]] in the Sluis sector. Sullust is in the [[Brema sector/Legends|Sullustan sector]]; Bothawui and Kothlis are in the [[Bothan Space/Legends|Bothan sector]]; Umgul is in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]; Mon Calamari is in the [[Calamari sector/Legends|Calamari sector]]. Additionally, the game mistakenly places the sector in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].

In the novel ''[[Jedi Trial]]'', the Sluis sector is incorrectly portrayed as being allied with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] instead of with the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

The name was first pronounced in ''[[Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire]]''.
